title: Drushei HaMalbush, Vol. 1: Kedusha Is Magic
subtitle: Memale kol almin, the Nation of Echad, and why we do not believe in magic.
html:
From Mikraei Kodesh, the Torah writings collected on liorsollyshachar.com.

A First Definition:

Kedusha: One of my Rebbeim in Ner Yisrael was asked at an oneg, "Is there anything of interest in the heightened draw people have toward matters of Chen?" He answered, "No, It's only exciting because people like magic." This statement is true.

Is it not the plot that One is reality, and One must prevail over the many? Is it not the case that the normative dynamics of earthly life are a form of process wielded to conceal that reality of memale kol almin, that nothing isn’t an active decision from Retzono Yitbarach, that nothing can be controlled by our synthetic retzonot, and that those decisions boil down to the unknowability of Ekye? Is it not the case that a miraculous rupture within a natural world order, or better yet a mode of seeing the data of our world through the internalized sobriety of Echad, must be a step in building the civilization of Echad? Is it not the case that our transformation-migration towards a world of Echad through the vehicle of Taryag will ultimately end in the answer to Ayeka? Is it not the case as well that there are two in love whose union is completely dependent on this very progression, where the reemergence in that chamber where Ayeka is asked is the same chamber where there separated two will meet again as one? Is it not the case that all of our avodah is organized by the implicit assumption of these plots, these narrative threads binding particularities into a gilui hayichud? If so, then what is Kedusha, this other reshut of Gavoha, this other space that is as much a different space as it is a dimension accessible where we already walk? What, then, is Ohr, the substance that fills any space which conforms to the shape of Echad, the substance that fills to the degree of that conformation? What exactly did you think the point of Rapach was if not to give life to a world prepared in perfect inperfection for our fixing, prepared as a perfect antagonist happy to die in Yirah and Ahava Al Kidush HaShem when we grind death through the teeth of eternity?

Despite these facts, the following is apparently a secret: Magic = Memale Kol Almin. ‘Memale kol almin’ is the gilui that the Ohr of Bli Gvul1 never left the Chalal. You think that by the time we get to this world, everything is cold, calcified and unchangeable. How can the heat of decisions made at the top truly penetrate the icy tundra of life in this dimension? Memale kol almin informs you that everything is made of the same unbound, molten Ratzon, changeable at any moment. When Kudsha Brich Hu is morid a deeper magnitude of His Presence2 in this dimension, how does earth react? With magic; unnatural and arcane behavior where water turns into blood, fire and ice entwine, an army is recruited from exotic and untamable animals, and the sea stands erect at attention like a general. What was the point of all that magic? All the mefarshim are masbir: He ingrained magic at the start of our story to teach us the sod of Emunah. The spectacle inheres within us the intuitive simplicity of En Od Milvado, i.e., the yesod of magic. At a lower altitude, that means Kudsha Brich Hu made the world, or in other words, Zecher leMa’aseh Bereshit. The higher altitude of that gilui is that He made the world for us, bishvil Yisrael hanikre reshit, or in other words Zecher LeYetziat Mitzrayim; for no other nation was magic performed to bring them out from another nation3. And why were we privileged with this special attention? Well, to bring us to Har Sinai, because the nukvah of Kudsha Brich Hu is none other than Kneset Yisrael, the Shechinah where Yisrael as a whole is mechunas keechad beshorsham. Har Sinai is where the Torah marries Kudsha Brich Hu VeYisrael VeOraita as Echad. It defined in terms of a marriage! The facticity of memale kol almin came to be megale that Yisrael is the Nation of Magic, the portal of magic in this world.

Between the walls of Yam Suf, the simplest of that nation saw visions Yechezkel didn't even see. The tribe of magic transitions into the civilization of magic, wielding in wars the magic word of Echad4. A fantasy society founded on the factuality of a fantastical reality, where the tribe of Echad becomes 12 with the kolel, gematria Echad. 12 tribes, 3 tribes to a camp, Degel Machane HaEsh, Mayim, Ruach, and Afar5, four otiot of shem Havaya Elokenu Havaya Echad. From the mountain-dwelling tribe of Ephraim to the trading seafarers of Zevulun — all sprawled out in the Eretz of Yisrael, the Land of Magic. The land is settled in a galaxy of mishpachot, sprawled around a central axis: the mountain6 on which the temple of the crouching lion7, regal and fiery, is surrounded by walls of bubbling turquoise and seafoam8. And the enchanting vision of Echad, the sister wing of Ahavat HaShem, is in fact a fiery lion from the chamber of magic itself!

There 70 wizards sit. And who is a wizard? He who knows the secret of memale kol almin, that there is nothing but the Ratzon, and how to see that fact in all matter and energy. The chachamim, besod enayim besod einei haeida, are therefore wizards because they see magic, teach us to see magic, and organize our lives by the light of magic they possess. The Ari is a wizard. Not because he could talk to birds and trees and see invisible things, but because he knows the secret of Echad, and with the secret of Echad, of course he could talk to the birds and trees and see invisible things! Furthermore, reality bends for those who are melumad in Echad, because anything is possible in the magical world of Echad if you merely take the time to sit in your seat and travel there. There remains an unbroken chain through the chachamim of one generation teaching the next the secret that the world never changes from generation to generation because the world is Echad. The first to teach the secret rode on donkeys, and the heirs of that secret drive in cars that need no gas to drive9, driving wherever magic is needed to help bring he who will ride as either as a prince or upon a donkey, the physicality of the world finally being controlled entirely by the rider.

That's why we don't believe in magic — we are magic. You can fool a goy, hamashul lachamor, besod chumriyut, besod kamotz asher tidfenu ruach10, with magic; any unidimensional shimmer of reality will dazzle a multidimensionally alienated donkey, but we need no shimmer to see the glow surrounding all things: En Od Milvado in an Olam Echad. What that means is that the chochmah of Echad is therefore magic. Chochmah demonstrates Echad through the in-sight that Havaya Achat is the blueprint of all things. A sefer of Torat HaAri is therefore magic.

So, what binds the wizards together, from the Noda BeYehuda to Rav Yehuda Fataye11? What motivates the wizard to engage in the wizardry of Tefillah (the whole point of which, as the Komarna is masbir, is to internalize memale kol almin), of Torah (vehashevota el levavecha that you live in Echad), and of Gemilut Chasadim (to build a world that houses the eventual revealed Presence12 of Echad)? The primary narrative of Echad: Romance. The motivation towards Chochmah cannot be the levush of magic, because that would be self-serving and adolescent, or in other words, making Torah a kardom lachtoch bah. The motivation is the plot to bring yichud between the girl lost in Ayeka back through the gates of Eden into the palace the Prince built for her. In that palace where He has waited for millennia, in the garden of simultaneous time, a Gan of Eden itself, waiting for her to walk back through those doors. In other words, what the Maharchu requires of those who are Ba BeSod (HaShem) Echad: you must only learn the limud al menat to do the kavanot and yichudim13.

Kedusha = Magic, because Magic is Beauty and Magic is Life. A magic moment is inadvertently a moment of truth and beauty, when worldly patterns and unity align their constellations forming a brief window into the world of Echad at the very place you stand. A davar shebikdusha is merely something belonging explicitly to the world of magic, in recognition of the invisible reshut gavoha, shem shamayim is chal alav. Kedusha is the Ohr that can live in kelim of Echad, Ohr that cannot go down with kelim of shevirah. Thus we find the Ohr stays put in Atzilut when those kelim are nishbar and die, Atzilut being the makom of Life, devoid of dinim and darkness.

In truth, however, ze leumat ze, in the Atzilut of klipah, is the antagonist in the romantic epic of Etz HaChaim. There are wizards of anti-magic, its own kind of magic because it weaponizes the miraculous feat of a world of one that succeeds in presenting itself in the illusion of many, taking that many and turning it against the Dorshei HaShem Echad. Wizards of entropy, disparity, and in their extreme, death, the opposite of Life because it says that an existence might be disconnected from its root in Chay Olamim; death is the opposite of Life because it attempts to substantiate the allegations that our world is truly one of disintegration. The fight, then, is for Life and magic to defeat entropy, death and anti-magic. Hopefully we will enter the millennia of magic, where the kol of Echad will holech vechazek meod in a full return of magic14, the olamot being nitaleh one madrega after the next, until the romance is complete and death will be digested by eternity.

In Igulim, Kudsha Brich Hu extended a Kav, the Vav of Shem Havaya, through which all the Ohr of Yud Kei will be brought to Vav Kei and the story will be complete. This is of course related to the issue of Yad al Kes Kah, a plotline continuing Midor Ledor.↩︎
